tagline.text: Birthplace of Bacolod's chicken inasal, a grilled-chicken food complex across from SM City Bacolod

location.label: Location
location.text: Father Ferrero Street, Reclamation Area, Bacolod, across from SM City Bacolod

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (especially busy during the MassKara Festival in October)

children.text: Manokan Country, meaning "chicken country" in the local language, is Bacolod's chicken inasal food complex. The old building was demolished in 2025, and its 24 stalls now operate from temporary stands at the SM City Bacolod transport hub, so check the latest situation before you go.

Manokan Country was a food complex dedicated to chicken inasal on Father Mauricio Ferrero Street in Bacolod's Reclamation Area. "Manokan" means "chicken country" in the local language, and the sign said exactly that. Inasal, charcoal-grilled chicken torn by hand and eaten with garlic rice, is the signature dish of Bacolod, and this was the best-known place to compare many versions of it in one spot. It sits directly across from SM City Bacolod, so it is easy to reach from anywhere in the city.

Its roots lie in the street-side chicken grilling that began near the Bacolod Public Plaza in the late 1970s and early 1980s. One article says that in 1979 the mayor built the complex to relocate inasal sellers so that grill smoke would not bother drivers and pedestrians, while another says the city government organized it as a dedicated food complex in the Reclamation Area in the 1980s. The years differ by source, so it is safe to say it took shape in the 1970s and 1980s. Bacolod's inasal became famous in connection with Cuadra Street from the 1970s, and on November 16, 2022 the city declared chicken inasal an important cultural property by ordinance.
There is an important change. In October 2023 the city of Bacolod and SM Prime Holdings signed a redevelopment contract for Manokan Country, a project worth about

on a 40-year lease. The old building was demolished in February 2025, and the 24 existing tenant stalls moved to a temporary site that opened in January 2025. The temporary site is at the SM City Bacolod transport hub, directly across from the old lot, and is described as having a shared dining area, a handwashing station and restrooms. A new building is under construction on the same lot and was reported to target a 2026 opening, but a May 2026 report said construction had been delayed by the fuel crisis. No opening date has been confirmed, so check the latest news before you visit.

So if you visit Manokan Country now, expect inasal eaten at temporary stands rather than the atmosphere of the old complex. Still, the stalls and the people who cook are the same, so it is worth having one meal here when you are in Bacolod. The Bacolod Chicken Inasal Festival in late May 2026 opened at this temporary site, which shows it is still used as the city's inasal center. Plans announced for the new building include an open-air plaza, a two-level beer garden, many hawker stalls and a hypermarket.

Chicken is marinated in calamansi, pepper, coconut vinegar, annatto and more, then grilled over hot charcoal while being basted with the marinade. Bacolod's version is described as mildly sour, while the Iloilo version is sweeter. One article says the chicken is marinated for nearly
24 hours

You can choose pechopak (breast with wing attached), paa (leg and thigh), pak-pak (wing), isol (chicken butt), and offal skewers such as liver and heart. Tastes differ, so starting with breast or leg is the safe choice.
Inasal usually comes with garlic rice, and the local way is to pour the yellow oil used for grilling the chicken over the rice. Many stalls are said to give extra chicken oil if you ask.
Dip the chicken in a sauce of calamansi juice, soy sauce and chili, or in sinamak, a spiced vinegar. Many people love the vinegar sauce, so try making both and compare.

blocks.title: The fun of eating by hand

children.text: Many stalls do not provide spoons and forks, and locals and travelers alike eat with their hands. There are places to wash up before and after, so there is no need to worry. In the old complex, MassKara masks were described as decorating the walls.

blocks.title: A plate of oysters and side dishes

children.text: Many locals order talaba (oysters) as an appetizer, along with street foods such as isaw (chicken intestines), atay (liver) and puso (rice in woven pouches). Oysters cost about ₱50–60 in older sources, so check current prices.

blocks.title: Each stall has its own character

children.text: Marinades and grilling methods differ from stall to stall, so even the same inasal tastes different. Aida's is the most famous and always crowded, Nena's Beth is described as relatively quieter, and names such as Nena's Rose and Cita's also come up often. The old building had 24 stalls.
Local news reports that Bacolod people come for inasal late at night and that some stalls stay open long, making it a popular hangover food. Keep it in mind as a place to go when you get hungry late.

items.title: Lunch inasal route
items.subtitle: A half day together with SM City Bacolod

children.text: Find the temporary Manokan Country at the SM City Bacolod transport hub. It is directly across from the old lot, so use the SM mall as your reference point.
Arrive early to avoid the lunch rush, look over the menus and displays at two or three stalls, and get a seat.
Order pechopak or paa with garlic rice, pour chicken oil over the rice, and add sinamak and calamansi sauce.
Add talaba or a skewer or two to try other cuts. If you are with others, sharing lets you taste a variety.
Wash your hands, then relax at SM City Bacolod or head into the city.
Lunch peak hours are described as crowded, so just before noon or well after it is quieter.

items.title: A day of eating and walking in Bacolod
items.subtitle: Historic sights and an inasal dinner

children.text: Walk around
San Sebastian Cathedral, Bacolod
and
Negros Occidental Provincial Capitol and Lagoon
in downtown Bacolod.
Have a light lunch and rest at your hotel to avoid the afternoon heat.
Move around the city and visit nearby sights such as
The Ruins
. Allow plenty of travel time.
Arrive at the temporary Manokan Country stalls before sunset for an early dinner. Local guides say about 5:30–6:30 p.m. is relatively quiet and 7–8 p.m. is the peak.
After dinner, buy souvenirs or snacks at SM City Bacolod and return to your hotel.
The Ruins is a drive from downtown Bacolod, so adjust the schedule to local traffic conditions.
Nonstop flights from Manila (NAIA) to Bacolod–Silay Airport (BCD) are described as taking about
1 hour 10 minutes–1 hour 30 minutes
in the air. Check the latest airline information and timetables.
The airport is in Silay City, about
15 km
from central Bacolod, and the drive is described as taking about
30–45 minutes
. It varies with traffic.

items.title: From the airport to the city

children.text: Take a taxi or ride-hailing car from the airport into Bacolod. Check fares locally.
Telling the driver "SM City Bacolod" or "Manokan Country" is usually understood.
Fast ferries connect Iloilo and Bacolod, and the crossing is described as taking about
1 hour–1 hour 30 minutes
, though some guides say it can approach 2 hours depending on the vessel and weather. Check the latest operator announcements and timetables.
From the Bacolod port to SM City, take a taxi or tricycle.
It is in front of SM City Bacolod, so it is easy to reach on foot, and you can come by taxi or ride-hailing car from anywhere in the city.
The temporary Manokan Country stalls are at the SM City Bacolod transport hub, close to the mall entrance.
The temporary location and news about the new building's opening may change, so check Google Maps and SM City Bacolod announcements.
Inasal does not depend on the season, so you can eat it any time of year. Since the temporary site is open-air in style, it is best to check for covered seating first during rainy periods.

During the MassKara Festival in October the city gets crowded, so arrange seats and transport early. The busiest times are around noon and 7–8 p.m., while early lunch or early dinner is relatively quiet. Stall hours differ and are described as running from early morning to late at night, so check the current hours of the stall you want.

Manokan Country is less a place with lodging than a food destination in the SM City Bacolod area. Downtown Bacolod has mid-range and budget hotels, malls and lodging around the Capitol, so staying near SM City or in the city center makes it easy to come by foot. Check specific lodging and rates by date on booking sites.

Inasal is the star of the food. Aida's is the most famous and always crowded, and in the old building it was described as stall 8, marked by a chicken statue. Nena's Beth is said to be quieter, and Nena's Rose was known as stall 13. Cita's has also been described as open 24 hours. However, these stall numbers and hours refer to the old building or are older descriptions, so they may have changed at the temporary site. Aida's is also described as having opened a standalone restaurant on San Juan Street in August 2024, so that is an option if the complex is crowded. Besides inasal, try local street foods and a plate of oysters.
Inasal is eaten by hand without a spoon, so check for a place to wash your hands and bring wet wipes. Locals eat with their hands too, so there is no need to feel awkward.
Mix a sauce of calamansi, soy sauce and chili, and have sinamak separately, dip the chicken in each, and pick the one you like.
One tip is to pour chicken oil over the garlic rice and add a little salt.
Lunch peak is crowded, so go just before noon or after 2 p.m.; for dinner, 5:30–6:30 p.m. is described as quieter.
If you are with others, order several cuts and share to compare them. One article wrote that a single piece of pechopak was enough for two people to share.

The temporary location and the new building's opening date may change, so before you go, check the latest status on Google Maps, SM City Bacolod announcements, the stalls' Facebook pages and similar sources.
Stall hours and menus differ, so if there is a particular stall you want, check its current hours first.
Stopping by SM City Bacolod as well lets you shop and rest, which makes the route convenient.

The old Manokan Country building was demolished in February 2025 and the stalls now operate from temporary stands at the SM City Bacolod transport hub, so check the current location before heading to the old address.
The temporary location, stall lineup and hours may change, so check the latest announcements just before you go.
Prices here mix older data with recent descriptions, so actual prices may differ. Ask for menu prices before ordering.
The site is close to open-air, so it can be hot during the day; choose an early dinner or a shaded seat.
Eat the chicken fully cooked and hot, and be careful with raw oysters or older food depending on how you feel.
Keep your belongings on you even while eating, and use a taxi or ride-hailing car for late-night travel.
The main cathedral in downtown Bacolod. Travel time varies with traffic, so check locally.
A downtown landmark with a lagoon park and the Capitol, good for a walk before or after a meal.
